// diagnostic

E2938

Invalid UI shortcut literal `{shortcut}`: {reason}

What

Invalid UI shortcut literal `{shortcut}`: {reason}

Why

`.cmd` is the checked command-key constructor, so its key is fixed before code generation and every tier receives the same shortcut metadata. During `jet check`, Jet reports this diagnostic.

Fix

Write a non-empty plain string literal, for example `.cmd("s")`; use `core.ui.host.shortcut` for a dynamic key.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E2938: tests/ui/ui_shortcut_cmd_dynamic_key.stderr.

Error [jet.InvalidShortcut]: Invalid UI shortcut literal `<expression>`: the key must be one plain string literal
  --> tests/ui/ui_shortcut_cmd_dynamic_key.jet:3:61
    |
  3 | fn shortcut_for(key: String) -> UIShortcut { UIShortcut.cmd(key) }
    |                                                             ^^^
 Why: `.cmd` is the checked command-key constructor, so its key is fixed before code generation and every tier receives the same shortcut metadata. During `jet check`, Jet reports this diagnostic.
 Fix: Write a non-empty plain string literal, for example `.cmd("s")`; use `core.ui.host.shortcut` for a dynamic key.
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E2938

Error [jet.UiServiceWithoutCapability]: UI host service `core.ui.host.shortcut` needs `UI.Shortcuts`.
  --> tests/ui/ui_shortcut_cmd_dynamic_key.jet:3:57
    |
  3 | fn shortcut_for(key: String) -> UIShortcut { UIShortcut.cmd(key) }
    |                                                         ^^^
 Why: The typed host row crosses an operating-system service boundary, so every tier must receive the same explicit package capability instead of discovering permission at runtime. During `jet check`, Jet reports this diagnostic.
 Fix: Add `UI.Shortcuts` to `authority.needs` in the package manifest, then rebuild.
